items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Mabel could cook all kind of Creole gumbo and everything. We had us a ball every day up there.

ctx.x: Did you get along with him all right?

Yeah, I got along with him fine. He used to have a white boy who comes to the house every day. He's a great writer. Him and I got to be good friends. His name is Charles Edward Smith. Yeah, I can say that. Boy, he was crazy about jelly. He was that, man, he was, and Mabel could cook all kind of Creole gumbo and everything. We had us a ball every day up there. I got a manuscript he gave me with a number. I was trying to figure, Mr. Russell, when you said finger breaker, I've got that manuscript, jelly, give it to…

Yeah, I don't have the record here anymore. I'll bring it down to Missouri. You sure you didn't have it in that pile that we picked out the other night? No, I didn't see it. You never didn't get those records.
